To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the release of ascorbate is impaired in the striatum of R6/2 Huntington's disease (R6/2 HD) mice during behavioral activation.

the striatal ascorbic acid levels are decreased in the R6/2 mouse model of Huntington's disease and that the ascorbic acid level is decreased during behavioral activation in R6/ 2 mice, but not in wild-type mice.
ascorbate release in the striatum of HD mice is dysregulated during behavioral activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurochemical and neurobehavioral consequences of a gene for HD, a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss and dysfunction of striatal neurons.
the role of extracellular ascorbate in the control of striatal function and the potential contribution of ascorbate to the pathophysiology of HD.
the role of extracellular ascorbate in the regulation of striatal function in the normal and diseased brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the striatal extracellular fluid of R6/2 HD mice is deficient in ascorbate, but not 3,4 dihydroxyphenylacetylic acid.
the ascorbic acid deficit is confined to the period of behavioural activation.
the R6/2 mouse model of Huntington's disease exhibits a significant deficit in the extracellular dynamics and release of ascorbic acid in the striatum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the R6/2 mouse model of Huntington's disease shows a progressive loss of striatal ascorbic acid release that is correlated with behavioral deficits.
ascorbic acid is a key antioxidant in the striatum and that its release is dysregulated in the R6/2 HD mouse model.
ascorbate release is impaired during periods of behavioral activation in the striatum of R6/2 HD mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ascorbate is not a reliable biomarker of the HD condition in mice.
the striatal ascorbic acid deficit is a consequence of the disease process and that it may be an important factor in the behavioral abnormalities of HD mice.
HD is associated with a deficit of extracellular ascorbate in the striatum of behaving mice.
